To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of antimicrobial dosages based on pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data is an important step towards the rational use of drugs and that the use of such dosages should lead to a reduction in the emergence of resistance and the use of drugs at the minimum effective dosage.

the pharmacodynamic/pharmacokinetic model of the sigmoid E(max) equation provides a basis for the development of dosage schedules for the treatment of infection in animals and that the application of population pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles to the development of such schedules will provide a rational basis for the prudent use and optimisation of antimicrobial agents.
the use of antimicrobial dosages based on population pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic principles is an effective approach to optimising antimicrobial therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of dosage schedules for antimicrobial agents, which will provide a basis for rational use.
the development and application of mathematical models for the optimisation of antimicrobial dosage regimens in order to provide a basis of the rational use of antibiotics in veterinary practice.
the development of a rational basis for the dosage regimen of antimicrobial drugs for animals, based on pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic principles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rational use of antibiotics should be based on the integration of pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data to develop dosage regimens that provide a therapeutic window that is wide enough to allow for the variation in both pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetcs of antimicrobial agents and the host.

the rational use of antibiotics should be based on the integration of pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data and that this can be best achieved by using the sigmoidal Emax equation and appropriate mathematical modelling and statistical analysis to take into account natural variation.
the dosage schedule for antimicrobial therapy should be based upon pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data, and that this is a prerequisite to the rational use of these drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the sigmoid Emax equation to integrate pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data, with appropriate statistical methods, is a useful tool in the design of optimal dosage regimens.

dosage schedules should provide high AUICS for drugs acting by time-dependent mechanisms, high AUICs and C(max)/MIC values for concentration-dependent drugs, and high AUICs for agents acting by a combination of concentration-dependent and time-dependent mechanisms.
dosage schedules should provide a basis for optimisation of the use of antimicrobial drug and should be used to guide the rational use of antibiotics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the E(max) model in combination with pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic data provides a rational basis for the design of dosage schedules for antimicrobial drugs.
we need a more rational approach to the use of antimicrobial therapy in animals.
it is important to use the right dose of antibiotics for the right animal, and to do so in a way that is both effective and sustainable for the future.
